name: piston_cylinder_water_constant_pressure
title: Piston-cylinder water heated at constant pressure (Cengel 3-55)
summary: A piston-cylinder holds 0.1 m3 of liquid water and 0.9 m3 of vapour in equilibrium at 800 kPa. Heat is added at constant pressure until 350 °C. The model computes the initial temperature, the total mass and the final volume. Textbook exercise Cengel 3-55.

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of 03-55.EES: 12 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 9. Maximum relative difference 2.20e-04 on T_init (170.406 °C vs 170.444 °C). m_tot rel 1.52e-05, V_final rel 8.18e-05. Enthalpy, entropy and work are absent from the stored solution.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in 03-55.EES (12 variables, EES X9.486)
verification.notes: 12 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001). Maximum over all common variables is 2.20e-04 on T_init (170.406 °C vs 170.444 °C). Also under rtol: rho_g and m_g 1.23e-04, rho_final 9.70e-05, V_final 8.18e-05, rho_f and m_f 2.09e-05, m_tot 1.52e-05, p, V_f, V_g and T_final 0. These residuals are the Water property formulation. The stored solution has no enthalpy or entropy, so no reference-state offset was measured; h[1], h[2], s[1] and s[2] exist only as diagram outputs. The source equation window does not compute the boundary work. The 9 CoolSolve-only names are x_1 and the diagram arrays P[i], h[i], T[i], s[i]. 3 iterations with .initials, 11 without. The diagram block does not change the 12 original variables (relative difference 0). density() warns that t=350 is read as 350 °C; that is T_final. The Fahrenheit hint did not print.
